base_member_text: [L75,L79-L83] (MED/unchecked-internal-io) Both list-directed and caller-formatted writes target a fixed-length display buffer without IOSTAT/IOMSG handling, so an invalid format or output longer than slen can raise a runtime I/O failure during logging.
audit_member_text: [L75,L79-L82] (MED/unchecked internal I/O failure) Every generated logger writes arbitrary caller content and format text into a fixed-length `display` buffer without `IOSTAT`, so an overlong record or invalid format can turn logging itself into a fatal runtime I/O error.

base_member_text: [L21-L25,L77] (LOW/kind-portability) Generated floating arguments use the nonstandard REAL*8 spelling instead of a selected or ISO_C_BINDING kind.
audit_member_text: [L21-L25,L77] (LOW/nonportable type declaration) Generated floating-point overloads use the nonstandard declaration `real*8`, whose size and generic-interface compatibility are compiler-dependent rather than tied to the project's declared real kind.

base_member_text: [L6-L12] (MED/duplicated-interface-source) The supported overload list is manually copied to another file rather than generated from a shared source, creating an explicit drift risk between implementations and their generic interface.

[L84-L87] (LOW/contradictory-contract) The comment says passing the trimmed display does not work, but the immediately following call passes trim(display), leaving the intended preservation of trailing buffer content unclear.
